Introduction and meaning
Personation of assessor. BNS restatement of IPC 232. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 232. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 268 is the rule on “Personation of assessor”. The section provides that . Whoever, by personation or otherwise, shall intentionally cause, or knowingly suffer himself to be returned, empanelled or sworn as an assessor in any case in which he knows that he is not entitled by law to be so returned, empanelled or sworn, or knowing himself to have been so returned, empanelled or sworn contrary to law, shall voluntarily serve as such assessor, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 268 exists so that “Personation of assessor” has a closed legal test in Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Perjury, screening, harbouring, false charge, and failing to appear on a bond.

hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 268 (Personation of assessor), Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) . Whoever, by personation or otherwise, shall intentionally cause, or knowingly suffer himself to be returned, empanelled or sworn as an assessor in any case in which he knows that he is not entitled by law to be so returned, empanelled or sworn, or knowing himself to have been so returned, empanelled or sworn contrary to law, shall voluntarily serve as such assessor, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 268 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 268 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

essentialIngredients: The commission of an act or omission falling within the statutory description of Personation of assessor.
The existence of the requisite culpable mental state (intention, knowledge, rashness, or negligence) prescribed under Section 268.
The absence of any statutory justification, exception, or lawful authority under Chapter III (General Exceptions).

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 268 constitutes a key component of Chapter XIV (Of False Evidence and Offences against Public Justice) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing personation of assessor. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of personation of assessor under Section 268 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 268.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 268 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 268 vs General Attempt: Section 268 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XIV; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.

Section 268 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 268 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of False Evidence and Offences against Public Justice.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 268 for conduct relating to personation of assessor.
Rule: Under BNS s. 268, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 268.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 268 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
